title: Stung into Action? Cyber Risk Management After a Breach
speaker: Emina Ademovic
description:

Abstract:
We study how cyber incidents reshape firms’ incentives to invest in cybersecurity and whether these investments pay off. Using novel measures from job postings and employee records, we document large and persistent post-incident improvements that move affected firms ahead of comparable firms in both cybersecurity human capital and technology. Firms with stronger pre-incident in-house cybersecurity capabilities experience smaller negative abnormal returns when incidents occur, whereas firms with greater reliance on external cloud infrastructure experience larger losses. Incident disclosure induces precautionary cybersecurity investment among similarly exposed firms, though firms' responses also raise reliance on common providers, contributing to systemic risk.

title: The Paris Agreement Ten Years Later: Navigating Climate Uncertainty and Tipping Points
speaker: Dirk Broeders, Francesco Paolo Mongelli
description:
Hybrid event.
To enter the virtual seminar room, please use the following login credentials:
Zoom URL:
https://uni-frankfurt.zoom-x.de/j/61866964299?pwd=z93TBpHIE0UwydYnrapz1NXfTq8XTt.1
Meeting ID: 618 6696 4299
Password: 416263
Abstract:
The climate crisis is an urgent, human‑driven, systemic challenge whose impacts are already unfolding through increasingly frequent and severe extreme events. Although the 2015 Paris Agreement marked a historic advance in global climate governance, implementation has lagged behind what is required to limit warming to well below 2 °C and pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5 °C by the end of the century. Emerging evidence of accelerating risks, interacting crises and potential tipping points underscores the possibility that climate change could become unmanageable if current trajectories persist. This paper advances three contributions. First, it takes stock of where the world stands and asks why humanity has so far failed to act decisively, highlighting the interaction of cognitive and political factors: a persistent awareness gap, competing policy priorities amid overlapping crises, and the absence of a sufficiently strong constituency for ambitious climate action. Second, it draws insights from three complementary climate‑policy frameworks—the climate policy trilemma, NGFS climate‑policy scenarios, and a precautionary approach—to clarify the trade‑offs and choices facing policymakers. Third, it systematically reviews a set of policy, financial and technological levers that can accelerate a just green transition, while reducing and potentially reversing climate risks. We argue that the climate crisis is evolving into a systemic “triple‑track” problem: (i) escalating and increasingly nonlinear physical risks; (ii) a persistent cognitive and awareness gap; and (iii) weak and unstable political incentives for more ambitious climate actions. We reassess the legacy of the Paris Agreement considering the substantial advances in technology, finance, data and modelling achieved over the past decade.

title: A Note on Endogenous Information Costs in Rational Inattention via Convex Duality
speaker: Stefan Behringer (Bielefeld University)
description:
Title:
A Note on Endogenous Information Costs in Rational Inattention via Convex Duality
Abstract:
The rational inattention literature employs two formulations of information costs: a hard constraint bounding mutual information by a Shannon capacity, and a soft constraint penalising mutual Information by a linear entropy penalty. We establish the structural relationship between these formulations via convex duality theory and develop its consequences. First, the hard-constraint value function, the Stratonovich/Shannon Value of Information (VoI), is the primitive object of rate distortion theory. The soft-constraint objective is its Fenchel conjugate, recoverable without parametric restriction, and the marginal cost of information is identified endogenously as the slope of the VoI; the linear entropy penalty is therefore a special case, not a maintained assumption. Second, the VoI generically depends on the full posterior distribution; it collapses to a function of posterior variance alone if and only if utility is quadratic, the prior is Gaussian, and optimal signals preserve conjugacy, three jointly necessary conditions. Third, the optimal signal Distribution takes an exponential form and generates a class of convex Risk measures; in a portfolio application, tail risk substantially amplifies information value relative to a mean-variance equivalent benchmark, a distinction that variance-based analysis cannot detect.
